topic: Complete comparator-parent Hall certificates for Gaussian feedback-module identification. Let K and O range over labeled noncomplete orientations of simple graphs on p≥4 vertices. For equal labeled outdegrees but different SCC partitions, define the local dependency digraph D_i(K,O): j→h when j is a K-child of i and h is both a K-parent of j and an O-neighbor of i. With P=ch_K(i)\ch_O(i), Q=ch_O(i)\ch_K(i), and Γ_i linking P to Q by D_i reachability, prove the all-size compatibility theorem H★: if every Γ_i(K,O) and Γ_i(O,K) has a perfect matching then SCC(K)=SCC(O). Equivalently, some order and vertex has a positive Hall deficiency, yielding a polynomial-time comparator-parent closed set L with a strict child-count gap. Prove that this certificate gives an explicit precision-Jacobian rank gap by the incoming-star minor, combine it with unequal-outdegree separation, and show a minimum-dimension compatible covariance-model selector generically recovers the true SCC partition. On each fixed compact Gaussian SEM family with stability, edge, eigenvalue, and cross-SCC covariance-separation margins, derive uniform covariance-minimum-distance consistency, honest split-sample SCC supersets, and union equilibrium-effect intervals. Consumer: within-regime Sachs et al. single-cell signaling-network analysis under an explicitly prospective homogeneous iid homoscedastic Gaussian oriented-network approximation; reciprocal arcs and regime pooling are outside scope. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The corrected precision-rank theorem was independently derived and its four-node rank-4-versus-5 witness recomputed exactly. Certificate optimization reduces exactly to |P| minus the maximum matching size in Γ_i, giving a polynomial search algorithm. H★ is proved for graph pairs differing in one outgoing row and for maximum-outdegree-one graphs. Exhaustive p=4 checks, the inherited complete p=5 check, a seeded 100,000-pair p=6–8 test, and 16,455 adversarial states through p=12 found no missing certificate; reciprocal-edge counterexamples confirm that the oriented-simple boundary matters. Searches found no corrected-certificate collision. The accessible arXiv-v1 construction leak is established, but the final journal equations remain unaudited and no broader correction is claimed. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove H★ for arbitrary multiple-tail disagreements by showing that two-sided local perfect matchings force equality of global SCC reachability, or produce another universal precision-variety separator. EARLY KILL TEST: Search dense-block SCC-discordant pairs for perfect matchings in every one of the 2p auxiliary graphs; one such pair refutes comparator-parent completeness and must pivot the run, though it is not by itself a counterexample to SCC identifiability. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_feedback_scc_rank_complete.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For every pair of labeled noncomplete simple orientations with equal labeled outdegrees but different strongly connected-component partitions, must some vertex admit a comparator-parent closed set with a strict child-count gap, equivalently a positive Hall deficiency in an associated reachability bipartite graph?

source_refs.claim: Conjecture 5.1 asks whether equal-outdegree noncomplete simple digraphs with different SCC partitions always admit a parentally closed child-count separator; only special cases and finite computations are established.
source_refs.author: Mathias Drton, Benjamin Hollering, Jun Wu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Drton, Hollering, and Wu prove the separator when one graph is acyclic and report exhaustive verification through five vertices plus sampled six-vertex tests, but their topological-minimal-disagreement argument does not extend when multiple disagreeing tails interact inside SCCs. Recasting parental closure as reachability and feasibility as bipartite matching makes certificate search polynomial, but leaves the central global implication unproved: two-sided local perfect matchings must force equality of mutual-reachability classes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would be either a theorem proving that two-sided local perfect matchings imply equality of SCC partitions for all such orientation pairs, with an explicit Hall-deficient vertex and closed set whenever they differ, or a finite labeled counterexample whose auxiliary graphs all have perfect matchings.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from homoscedastic observational identification to Jacobian-matroid certificates and then isolates the SCC-sensitive graph conjecture.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Feedback invalidates DAG identification arguments -> homoscedastic precision models have graph-dependent Jacobian matroids -> parentally closed child-count gaps distinguish model varieties -> establish the conjectured separator for every SCC-discordant pair.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a precision-coordinate set whose parameterization Jacobian has graph-dependent rank using incoming-star columns associated with a parentally closed set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired Hall witness is intended to supply exactly the closed set needed by this Jacobian-rank separation argument.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert generic SEM identifiability into vertex-disjoint path systems and certify the graphical condition through polynomial-time flow or matching arguments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems require translating a global algebraic-rank assertion into a Hall-type combinatorial path system with controlled endpoint conflicts.

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate uniform sample-covariance concentration through conditional-variance comparisons to obtain finite-sample graph-order recovery under eigenvalue and signal margins.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After population SCC identification, analogous covariance-perturbation and margin bounds can support an attaining SCC selector.

open_problems.open_problem: On each fixed compact stable homoscedastic Gaussian feedback-SEM family separated by positive edge, eigenvalue, and cross-SCC covariance-model margins, can covariance minimum-distance selection be made uniformly SCC-consistent and combined with sample splitting to give honest SCC supersets and union confidence intervals for equilibrium total effects?

source_refs.claim: The paper establishes generic algebraic distinguishability through graph-dependent precision-Jacobian ranks but does not supply uniform model-selection or post-selection inference guarantees.
source_refs.author: Mathias Drton, Benjamin Hollering, Jun Wu

source_refs.claim: Its penalized-likelihood global minimizer is shown asymptotically to recover a quasi-equivalence class under generalized faithfulness and an additional minimality assumption.
source_refs.author: Amiremad Ghassami, Alan Yang, Negar Kiyavash, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: The paper constructs confidence sets for DAG causal orderings and derives ancestral supersets and causal-effect intervals by residual-bootstrap goodness-of-fit inversion.
source_refs.author: Y. Samuel Wang, Mladen Kolar, Mathias Drton
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: It demonstrates undercoverage from treating a learned homoscedastic causal graph as known and develops test-inversion confidence regions in the bivariate case.
source_refs.author: David Strieder, Tobias Freidling, Stefan Haffner, Mathias Drton

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic algebraic distinguishability only excludes lower-dimensional intersections and gives no uniform statistical separation near them. Cyclic precision models may be curved or singular, equilibrium effects depend nonlinearly on the inverse structural operator, and selection followed by ordinary intervals reuses the covariance noise. Uniform recovery therefore requires explicit compactness, stability, eigenvalue, edge, and between-SCC model-distance margins, simultaneous control of distances to finitely many covariance varieties, and an inference construction that retains the true SCC candidate before unioning graph-specific effect intervals.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would provide a uniform probability bound for a covariance-minimum-distance SCC selector and a split-sample theorem guaranteeing coverage of the true SCC partition by a graph-valued superset and of every predeclared equilibrium total effect by the union of compatible-model intervals.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames causal-discovery uncertainty as a confidence set over structural objects and propagates that set into relation and effect statements.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A point graph estimate hides structural uncertainty -> invert model goodness-of-fit tests to retain plausible causal structures -> summarize retained structures by honest relation supersets -> propagate them into equilibrium-effect intervals.

method_exemplars.technique: Use graph-specific precision parameterizations and Jacobian-rank differences to establish population covariance-model separation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed selector compares these cyclic homoscedastic covariance models, with SCC rather than full-graph recovery as its target.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert residual-bootstrap goodness-of-fit tests over structural candidates and post-process the accepted set into relation supersets and effect intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Replacing DAG orderings by cyclic SCC and covariance-model candidates gives the closest existing blueprint for honest graph-valued uncertainty.

method_exemplars.technique: Use resampling and screening to retain valid graphs, then form a union of graph-specific asymptotically normal intervals for the fixed true causal effect.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired union equilibrium-effect interval has the same logical requirement that structural screening retain a representation of the true model with high probability.

open_problems.open_problem: For equal-outdegree noncomplete orientations having the same SCC partition and tying on every parentally closed child-count test, characterize a universally checkable precision-Jacobian or vanishing-polynomial separator, or exhibit a pair whose homoscedastic Gaussian covariance varieties coincide.

source_refs.claim: Conjecture 5.2 proposes generic identification of all noncomplete graphs, while Example 5.3 gives same-SCC graphs that defeat every parentally closed count test although their Jacobian matroids still differ.
source_refs.author: Mathias Drton, Benjamin Hollering, Jun Wu

source_refs.claim: The paper characterizes distribution equivalence of cyclic linear Gaussian graphs using support rotations, parent operations, and cycle reversions, distinguishing it from weaker quasi-equivalence.
source_refs.author: Amiremad Ghassami, Alan Yang, Negar Kiyavash, Kun Zhang

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parentally closed-set construction reads only a restricted family of incoming-star Jacobian minors and ceases to distinguish graphs once SCC partitions and all local counts agree. Drton, Hollering, and Wu show that failure of this test does not imply model collision—their six-node example still has different matroids—while the distribution-equivalence operations of Ghassami et al. act on a broader precision-factor support representation. No known criterion connects those operations to a polynomial complete separator for all remaining noncomplete orientations, and equality of algebraic matroids alone would not imply equality of covariance varieties.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would give a necessary-and-sufficient, effectively checkable characterization of equality of homoscedastic Gaussian covariance varieties for same-SCC noncomplete orientations, with an explicit distinguishing Jacobian minor or vanishing polynomial whenever the varieties differ.

writing_exemplar.why: Its Example 5.3 exposes the precise boundary at which the existing local certificate fails while stronger algebraic information remains.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Local degree tests separate many graphs -> parentally closed sets enlarge the separating family -> same-SCC examples defeat all such local counts -> full noncomplete-graph identification requires a stronger algebraic separator.

method_exemplars.technique: Factor the precision matrix and characterize equality through support-preserving orthogonal rotations, parent exchanges, reductions, and cycle reversions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These transformations expose distributional equivalences invisible to a restricted family of Jacobian minors and may furnish the missing within-SCC characterization.

method_exemplars.technique: Compare coordinate-projection algebraic matroids through symbolic Jacobian ranks instead of computing full Gröbner bases.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested separator must extend this tractable rank-witness approach to cases where all incoming-star minors tie.

method_exemplars.technique: Use expected model dimension to justify Gaussian score comparison and greedy structure search over simple cyclic models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A complete within-SCC variety characterization would make dimension-correct score comparison an attainable estimator for newly distinguishable models.

open_problems.open_problem: With a known partition of variables into error-variance blocks, characterize when the SCC partition of a noncomplete simple cyclic linear Gaussian SEM is identifiable from observational covariance and determine the weakest blockwise-homoscedasticity pattern that preserves SCC recovery.

source_refs.claim: The paper characterizes distribution equivalence under groupwise equal error variances only for recursive linear SEMs and represents the resulting DAG class by a CPDAG.
source_refs.author: Jun Wu, Mathias Drton
source_refs.venue: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Information Theory

source_refs.claim: The cyclic algebraic-matroid criteria assume one common error variance for every vertex and do not treat multiple variance blocks.
source_refs.author: Mathias Drton, Benjamin Hollering, Jun Wu

open_problems.why_unsolved: The occupied literatures leave a specific missing corner: partial homoscedasticity has a DAG equivalence theory, whereas cyclic Jacobian certificates use one common scale. With several block scales, the precision parameterization gains one scale row per block, labeled outdegrees no longer induce the same diagonal-rank comparisons across blocks, and the DAG characterization relies on acyclic covered-edge transformations. Neither argument determines whether mutual reachability remains recoverable or which variance blocks must intersect feedback modules.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would provide a necessary-and-sufficient covariance-equivalence or SCC-recoverability criterion for cyclic SEMs with a prescribed variance partition, including a recovery map or explicit nonidentifiable pair for every block pattern and a finite-sample attaining selector under separation margins.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates groupwise equality as an interpretable bridge between arbitrary variances and the restrictive all-equal assumption.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Arbitrary error variances leave broad observational equivalence -> all-equal variances identify substantially more structure -> real variables may form equal-scale blocks -> characterize exactly what partial equality identifies in feedback systems.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode a known variance partition in the Gaussian SEM model and characterize equality through block-restricted distributional constraints and graph transformations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination changes the graph class from DAGs to cyclic orientations while retaining the source paper's block-scale parameterization.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze the precision-parameterization Jacobian combinatorially and exhibit coordinate subsets with graph-dependent ranks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The first proof step that changes is replacing the single common-scale row by block-specific scale rows and determining which incoming-star minors remain separating.

method_exemplars.technique: Identify total effects without fully identifying the DAG under partial homoscedasticity and invert structural uncertainty into effect confidence regions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides nearby inference machinery for a block-homoscedastic target that can be adapted after cyclic SCC-level equivalence is characterized.

literature_map:
Richardson (1997, International Journal of Approximate Reasoning) gives a polynomial characterization of d-separation Markov equivalence for directed cyclic graphs, but this equivalence ignores non-CI Gaussian information.
Foygel, Draisma, and Drton (2012, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1107.5552) turn generic linear-SEM parameter identification into polynomially checkable half-trek and path-system conditions.
Peters and Bühlmann (2014, JMLR, arXiv:1205.2536) establish full observational identification for homoscedastic linear Gaussian DAGs.
Chen, Drton, and Wang (2019, Biometrika, arXiv:1807.03419) derive variance-ordering algorithms and finite-sample covariance-concentration guarantees, with acyclicity driving the recursion.
Ghassami, Yang, Kiyavash, and Zhang (2020, ICML, arXiv:1910.12993) replace cyclic Markov equivalence by distribution and quasi-equivalence and give an asymptotically consistent penalized score under additional assumptions.
Améndola, Dettling, Drton, Onori, and Wu (2020, UAI, arXiv:2006.05978) establish expected dimension and score-based learning for simple cyclic linear Gaussian mixed-graph models.
Bongers, Forré, Peters, and Mooij (2021, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1611.06221) show that cyclic causal semantics require solvability conditions for unique observational and interventional distributions.
Drton, Hollering, and Wu (2025, Advances in Applied Mathematics, arXiv:2308.01821) introduce precision-Jacobian matroid separators and state the exact SCC-sensitive parentally closed-set conjecture.
Their Example 5.3 identifies a second frontier: same-SCC graphs can defeat all parentally closed count tests while retaining different Jacobian matroids.
Wu and Drton (2023, IEEE JSAIT, arXiv:2308.08959) characterize partial-homoscedastic equivalence for DAGs, leaving cyclic block-variance recovery unaddressed.
Yi and Lee (2024, AISTATS) propose Filter-Rank-Prune for cyclic Gaussian graphs, but do not give a complete SCC identification or inference theorem.
Strieder et al. (2021, UAI, arXiv:2106.05694), Wang, Kolar, and Drton (2025, JASA, arXiv:2305.14506), Gradu et al. (2025, JASA, arXiv:2208.05949), and Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2025, Biometrika, arXiv:2405.06763) expose post-discovery undercoverage and supply test-inversion, randomized, bootstrap, and union-interval templates centered on DAG settings.
Mokhtarian et al. (2023, JMLR, arXiv:2205.10083) give worst-case cyclic experiment-design bounds, while Sharifian et al. (2025, NeurIPS, arXiv:2509.21423) exploit perfect matchings and adaptive submodularity under non-Gaussian noise.
Sachs et al. (2005, Science, DOI:10.1126/science.1105809) use single-cell measurements and molecular perturbations to orient a signaling network; their pooled intervention design is not evidence for a within-regime iid homoscedastic Gaussian feedback model and remains only a prospective application boundary.
